limitations: No licence statement appears on the TranStats download page itself; the public-domain designation is taken from BTS's own data-portal metadata for T-100-derived products plus 17 U.S.C. 105, with BTS requiring source citation. Anyone re-publishing should carry the BTS credit line rather than assert a CC0 dedication over the upstream data.

The download path is an ASP.NET form postback with view-state tokens, not a stable static file URL; eleven annual pulls must be scripted, and the interface could change. The 'Prezipped File' option is the documented fallback.

The label treats a seasonal suspension as an exit whenever the carrier performs no departures in the three-month anniversary window, so genuinely seasonal routes launched in the wrong season are systematically coded as failures.

Corporate events are confounded with route failure: mergers, certificate transfers and UniqueCarrier re-coding make an acquired carrier's routes vanish from the panel and be labelled discontinued even where service continued under another code.

Entry episodes are not independent within carrier or within airport: a carrier that shuts down fails all of its new routes at once, and a hub's entry cohort shares the same local demand shock. Row counts overstate the effective number of independent events.

Domestic U.S. certificated carriers only: foreign-carrier entries, non-scheduled/charter service (classes L/N/P/Q/R/V) and all-cargo-only service are excluded, so results do not describe the whole market.

T-100 coverage of very small commuter operators is uneven and reporting practices vary, which is partly why the >=8 departures-in-entry-month rule is used; that rule also removes genuine but very thin new services.

City-market aggregation deliberately hides airport-level shifts within a metro (e.g. a move from one metro airport to another counts as continuous service), which is a definitional choice, not a measurement of airport-level survival.

All entries after 2018-12 are excluded because their anniversary windows cross the 2020 schedule collapse, so the task describes pre-2019 market structure and is a retrospective, current-vintage construction rather than proof of what an operator could have computed live in 2013.
No performance metrics were computed and none should be inferred from this selection; the base rate and the entry counts above are estimates pending construction.
No historical vintages or full-row availability ledger are supplied; the current TranStats snapshot is used and training_label_timing is unverified.
No publisher publication schedule was supplied; a conservative 90-day administrative availability lag is assumed for timing metadata and is not a measured publication date.
The source has month-level dates only; the qualification event cluster is the carrier identity, not a day-level event timestamp.
T-100 publication lag is not documented in the supplied evidence; no zero-day publication date is invented.
Absence of a T-100 pair-month row is treated as zero performed departures only after global month coverage and missing-DepPerformed checks; missing feature values are blank rather than zero.
City-market aggregation hides airport-level shifts inside a metro.
Seasonal suspensions, mergers, certificate transfers and carrier re-coding can be coded as route exits.
Entries are not independent within a carrier or hub; route counts overstate independent events.
The frozen population is U.S. certificated carriers and Class F scheduled service; foreign carriers, non-scheduled classes and all-cargo-only service are not described.
Small commuter coverage is uneven and the at-least-8-departures rule removes very thin services.
Entries after 2018-12 are excluded because their anniversary windows cross the 2020 schedule collapse.
The label uses all-class DepPerformed over M+12 through M+14 as frozen; if only scheduled passenger service is intended, the semantics differ.
The base rate is measured by construction and is not assumed.
No uncertainty interval; observed differences do not establish universal headroom

paragraphs: When a U.S. certificated carrier starts scheduled passenger nonstop service on a domestic city market pair it has not served in the previous 12 months, will that service still be operating in the anniversary quarter 12-14 months later?

Population: Eligible unit is one carrier by directed origin city market by directed destination city market entry episode. In month M the carrier reports Class F scheduled passenger/cargo service, total Passengers greater than zero and total DepPerformed at least 8, and the same carrier performed zero departures on that directed pair in every month M-12 through M-1. Both endpoints are U.S. airports or territories in the U.S. carriers domestic T-100 table. The carrier is a U.S. certificated reporting carrier identified by UniqueCarrier. Months M+12 through M+14 must exist in the downloaded panel. Only entry months inside the frozen train eval and holdout windows are kept; no outcome condition enters eligibility. Rows lacking a fully reported anniversary window are omitted as unknown labels, never relabeled negative.

Target: label = 1 if the carrier's summed DepPerformed (departures performed) on the directed city-market pair over months M+12, M+13 and M+14 equals 0, i.e. the route is not operating at its one-year anniversary; label = 0 if any departures were performed in that three-month anniversary window.

Prediction time: Ninety days after the end of entry month M, after the monthly T-100 compilation for M is assumed available. Only T-100 records for months at or before M may enter features; months after M are unseen.

Splits: Frozen chronological boundaries by entry month, set before any modelling: train = entries in 2011-01..2014-06; eval (validation) = 2015-10..2016-09; holdout = 2018-01..2018-12. Two 15-month embargo gaps drop all entries in 2014-07..2015-09 and 2016-10..2017-12 so that no split's 14-month label window overlaps the next split's decision period. No entries after 2018-12 are used at all, because their anniversary windows fall inside the COVID-19 schedule collapse and would change the label's meaning. Data pulls cover 2010-01..2020-02 only.
Outcome horizon: 12 to 14 months after the entry month (three-month anniversary window).

Inputs: distance_miles: Reported nonstop segment distance between the two airports in statute miles; modal value across Class F entry-month rows; time-invariant proxy for block time, fuel burn and yield pressure.; entry_calendar_month: Calendar month of entry month M from 1 to 12; captures seasonality of route launches.; carrier_departures_prior_12m: Total DepPerformed by the carrier over months M-11 through M across all service classes reported in T-100; carrier scale and financial capacity proxy.; carrier_active_pairs_prior_12m: Number of distinct directed city-market pairs on which the carrier performed departures in months M-11 through M; network breadth.; carrier_route_attrition_prior_12m: Share of the carrier directed pairs that operated in month M-12 but had zero departures in month M; point-in-time rate at which this carrier abandons routes.; origin_market_departures_prior_12m: All-carrier, all-class departures performed at the origin city market over months M-11 through M; origin hub or station size.; dest_market_departures_prior_12m: All-carrier, all-class departures performed at the destination city market over months M-11 through M; destination size.; competing_carriers_prior_3m: Number of other UniqueCarrier codes with performed departures on the directed city-market pair in months M-3 through M-1; incumbent competition the entrant faces.; pair_departures_prior_3m: All-carrier, all-class departures performed on the directed city-market pair in months M-3 through M-1; zero indicates a previously unserved market rather than a contested one.; entry_month_departures: The carrier own Class F DepPerformed on the directed pair in month M; intensity of the initial schedule commitment.; entry_month_seats_per_departure: Class F Seats divided by Class F DepPerformed on the pair in month M; aircraft gauge committed to the route.; entry_month_load_factor: Class F Passengers divided by Class F Seats on the pair in month M; first-month demand realisation.; carrier_new_at_origin: 1 if the carrier performed zero departures at the origin city market in months M-12 through M-1, meaning the route also opens a new station; 0 if any departures occurred.; carrier_new_at_dest: 1 if the carrier performed zero departures at the destination city market in months M-12 through M-1; 0 if any departures occurred.
